# The native-titlebar popup drag path has zero coverage, and produces no drop-zone previews in the Workstation

## Context

Reported by @tobiu 2026-09-01 against the Workstation on `dev@2f8fc79792`: *"Pop-out => grab the popup header, move it around => ZERO drop zone previews. does only re-integrate on close. REALLY REALLY bad."*

He also corrected two wrong readings of mine before this ticket existed, and both corrections shape its scope:

1. I claimed cross-window previews were unbuilt and pointed at #17578. **Wrong** — they work and are e2e-proven.
2. I then claimed this was an unfiled `G3` lane on epic #15239. **Also wrong** — the feature is implemented.

**Live latest-open sweep** at 2026-09-01T17:29Z plus a Memory Core sweep (`query_summaries`) over the popup/cross-window decision space, which is what surfaced the prior art my issue-title greps had missed.

## Why it works in the tests but not by hand

The proven path is **`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL.spec.mjs`** (video mode: `NEO_FILM_TAKE=1`, *"replays the identical assertions with on-glass compositing"*). It asserts, at `:1017` and `:1026`, *"target choices remain visible"* and *"target preview remains visible beside proxy"*.

Its own contract explains why that does not cover the reported gesture:

> *"Every gesture input is Playwright's trusted `page.mouse` stream. CDP only controls physical native window bounds so the matrix is deterministic."*
> *"CDP is deliberately only the physical-window adapter; **no gesture or dock semantic rides it**."*

So every existing arm drives the **pointer** path and merely *stages* window positions. The reported gesture is the only one that goes through `DragCoordinator#onWindowPositionChange` (`src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:1034`) — whose JSDoc says it exists precisely for this:

> *"Handles geometry updates for native OS-titlebar popup reintegration... where the browser does not emit pointer move/up events. The current candidate target **renders continuous hover preview per update**; a terminal detached popup reintegrates only after it remains over a remote dashboard target long enough to satisfy the settle/dwell intent contract."*

**This is an implemented feature with zero end-to-end coverage.** That is the defect's root condition: nothing exercises it, so nothing caught its regression.

## Root cause (measured 2026-09-01, supersedes the earlier branch table)

`Neo.main.addon.WindowPosition` arms its 20ms movement poll on one signal only: a `mouseout` whose `toElement` is null, the event a pointer produces when it travels from page content onto the OS titlebar. The header-action pop-out births the vessel with its titlebar directly under the pointer that clicked the action, so the hand grabs the titlebar without the cursor ever entering popup content. **No `mouseout` fires in the popup realm, the poll never arms, no geometry is published.** `manager.Window` keeps the birth rect, the candidate hit-test reads a stationary centre, nothing previews, and reintegration is reachable only through the close path, which needs no geometry.

Three arms of one probe on `dev@0659b0e42d`, identical except for the trigger (CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds` as the physical-window adapter, four steps onto the main window's centre):

| trigger in the popup realm | poll armed | `manager.Window` follows | previews per step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none — titlebar grabbed from outside content | **no** | **no** | **0 · 0 · 0 · 0** |
| synthetic `mouseout`, no `toElement` (my earlier probes) | yes | yes | 0 · 0 · 0 · 1 → reintegration |
| real CDP pointer enters content, leaves through the top edge | yes | yes | 0 · 0 · 1 · 1 → vessel closed |

Downstream control in the failing arm: one direct `publishGeometry()` afterwards moved the manager rect to the live screen position, so the publish path and `onWindowPositionChange` are intact. Branches 1–3 of the original table never execute because `onWindowPositionChange` is never called; branch 4 was "cleared" only under a synthetic trigger the human gesture does not produce. The pointer-path specs never saw this because `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` calls `publishGeometry()` by hand after every CDP move, and a pointer tear-out always crosses popup content before the titlebar. A probe that supplies the trigger cannot test whether the trigger occurs.

Full measurement trail: the root-cause comment below (2026-09-01).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An e2e arm drives the native-titlebar path — not a `page.mouse` gesture — and asserts a drop-zone preview renders in the target realm while the popup is over it. It must fail on current `dev`.
- [ ] The arm distinguishes its synthetic trigger from the production path in a comment, and asserts the trigger actually armed the poll, so a probe that never armed cannot report green.
- [ ] Whichever of branches 1–3 bails is identified **by measurement**, with the reading's positive control stated. `Object.keys()` on a `Map` does not count.
- [ ] Reintegration is asserted to happen while the popup is *over* the target under the settle/dwell contract — not only on close.
- [ ] The pointer path stays green: `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` (all matrix cells) and `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` are unaffected.
- [ ] The fix does not introduce a second gesture system. Per ADR 0029 §2.3, previews go through the owner's landed preview machinery and drops through `previewToOperation()` → commit.

## Out of Scope

- Maximize arming order (#18027).
- `lock` remaining opt-in — a stated #18014 decision, not a defect.
- Multi-display behaviour: `window.moveTo` is unpermissioned across displays, per the D#15204 audit.

Refs #17836 · #15239 · #18014

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-01T17:46:41Z

## Root cause isolated: the popup's geometry never reaches `Neo.manager.Window`

Driven to a measurement. Three of the four branches are now settled, and the bail is **upstream of all of them**.

### Cleared

| # | branch | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `getNativeWindowDragSource(windowId)` | **CLEARED.** Called directly with the popup's real Neo windowId, it returns a live drag source — `draggedItem`, `mounted: true`, matching `windowId`. The main window's id correctly returns `null`, which is the discrimination: a broken `callMethod` would have failed both identically. |
| 4 | the 20ms position poll arming | **CLEARED.** In the popup realm `WindowPosition.intervalId` is `false` before and `true` after a `mouseout` with no `toElement` — the exact condition `onMouseOut` tests — and it is **still armed** at the end of the gesture. |

### The actual defect

With the poll armed, walking the popup's centre onto the main window's dock centre in four steps produces **zero previews at every step**:

```
[realPath] [{step:0.25, preview:0}, {step:0.5, preview:0}, {step:0.75, preview:0}, {step:1, preview:0}]
```

(selector `.neo-dock-preview-affordance`, the same one the proven pointer-path arm asserts on.)

And the control explains why:

```
[popupRectInWorker]  {x: 55, y: 117, width: 320, height: 417}     ← unchanged
[allRectsAfter]      [[main, 22, 22, 1280], [popup, 55, 117, 320]] ← popup never moved
```

**`Neo.manager.Window` still holds the popup's original rect** after the window physically moved. So `getNativeWindowDropCandidate` computes `popupRect.x + width/2` from a position that never changes — no candidate resolves, `updateNativeHover` renders nothing, and the settle/dwell contract can never be satisfied. That is both halves of the report: no previews, and reintegration only through the close path, which does not depend on geometry.

### Instrument validated before blaming the product

`Browser.setWindowBounds` could plausibly move a window without updating `screenX`/`screenY`, which would make the whole probe void. Measured directly:

```
[screenBefore] {screenX: 22,  screenY: 22}
[screenAfter ] {screenX: 400, screenY: 260}
[cdpBounds   ] {left: 400,    top: 260}
```

They track exactly. So the browser *is* reporting the new position to the page, the poll *is* running, and the geometry still does not arrive in the App Worker. **The publish path from the popup realm's `WindowPosition` addon to `manager.Window` is where this fails.**

Branch 2 (the `parking`/`embodied`/`settling-*` phase guard) is untested and now moot for triage: with geometry that never updates, `onWindowPositionChange` has nothing to act on regardless of phase.

### Correction to this ticket's own framing

The body says branch 1 is "open — its data source is confirmed populated, but the registry lookup itself is unmeasured". It is now measured and cleared. The body's branch table is superseded by the one above.

Next: instrument `checkMovement` → `onWindowPositionChange` in the popup realm to find where the update is dropped — whether the poll's own comparison suppresses it, or the message never leaves the realm.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-01T19:59:14Z

## Root cause, corrected: the poll that publishes popup movement is never armed by this gesture

My comment above was wrong about *where* the geometry is lost. The publish path from the popup realm to `Neo.manager.Window` is intact. What never happens is the **poll** that would call it.

### The mechanism

`Neo.main.addon.WindowPosition` arms its 20ms movement poll on exactly one signal: a `mouseout` whose `toElement` is null, the event a pointer produces when it travels from page content onto the OS titlebar. The header-action pop-out births the vessel with its titlebar directly under the pointer that just clicked the action. The hand grabs the titlebar without the cursor ever entering the popup's content, so **no `mouseout` fires in the popup realm, the poll never arms, and no geometry is ever published**. `manager.Window` keeps the birth rect, `getNativeWindowDropCandidate` hit-tests a stationary centre, nothing previews, and reintegration is only reachable through the close path, which needs no geometry. Both halves of the report, one cause.

### How it was measured

Three arms of one probe, identical except for the trigger, on `dev@0659b0e42d`, Playwright driving CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds` as the physical-window adapter (`manager.Window` rect, poll counters and preview count read after each of four steps):

| trigger in the popup realm | poll armed | publishes | `manager.Window` follows | previews |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no pointer event at all (titlebar grabbed from outside content) | **no** | 0 | **no** (birth rect kept) | **0 / 0 / 0 / 0** |
| synthetic `mouseout` with no `toElement` (what my earlier probes dispatched) | yes | 4 | yes | 0 / 0 / 0 / 1, then reintegration |
| real CDP pointer entering content, then leaving through the top edge | yes | 3 | yes | 0 / 0 / 1 / 1, then the vessel closed |

Positive control for the downstream path in the failing arm: one direct `publishGeometry()` afterwards moved the manager rect to the current screen position. So the branch table in the body was asking the wrong question: branches 1–3 never run, because `onWindowPositionChange` is never called. Branch 4 was "cleared" only under a synthetic trigger the human gesture does not produce.

### Why the pointer-path specs never saw it

`WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` calls `WindowPosition.publishGeometry()` by hand after every CDP move, and the pointer tear-out path always crosses popup content before the titlebar. Neither exercises the poll's arming condition. A probe that *supplies* the trigger cannot test whether the trigger occurs.

### Fix shape (PR follows)

`WindowPosition` gains a reactive `observeMovement_` config that owns the poll independent of pointer travel; the Workstation opts both render targets in (`observeResize` already rides the same calls). The e2e arm drives the gesture with **no** pointer event in the popup realm, asserts the poll is armed by config with a zero `mouseout` count, and asserts previews plus reintegration under the dwell contract through the production poll alone.

One adjacent observation, evidenced while building the arm and out of this ticket's scope: the detach projection's `refreshCrossWindowParticipation` re-registers the main target a few hundred milliseconds after the pop-out commit, and a native candidate claimed before that refresh dies with the zone it claimed (the coordinator tolerates registration refreshes only in the `settling-target` phase). A human grabs the titlebar long after that refresh lands; the arm waits for it explicitly. Noted in the PR.

— Vega (Fable 5.1, Claude Code) 🌿
